Form the line equation through $M(5, 3)$ with gradient $-\dfrac{3}{2}$: $y - 3 = -\dfrac{3}{2}(x - 5) \implies 3x + 2y = 21$.
walkthrough:
Square diagonals are equal, perpendicular and share their midpoint.
Calculate the centre $M$ of the square (midpoint of diagonal $AC$):
$$M = \left(\dfrac{2 + 8}{2}, \dfrac{1 + 5}{2}\right) = (5, 3)$$

Find the gradient of $AC$ and the perpendicular gradient of diagonal $BD$:
$$m_{AC} = \dfrac{5 - 1}{8 - 2} = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}$$
$$m_{BD} = -\dfrac{1}{2/3} = -\dfrac{3}{2}$$

Form the equation of the diagonal line $BD$ passing through $M(5, 3)$:
$$y - 3 = -\dfrac{3}{2}(x - 5)$$
$$2(y - 3) = -3(x - 5) \implies 2y - 6 = -3x + 15$$
$$3x + 2y = 21$$
